newsitem.title: USA: Standard & Poor's introduces REIT Composite index.
newsitem.headline: Standard & Poor's introduces REIT Composite index.

text.p: Citing growing demand, Standard & Poor's Financial Information Services group on Thursday introduced a new composite index designed to track the performance of Real Estate Investment Trusts, commonly known as REITs.
The new index consists of 100 REIT's and covers more than 80 percent of the securitized real estate market, S&P said in a statement.
Issues have to be traded on a major U.S. stock exchange to qualify and must have a market value of at least $100 million, the group added.

"The REIT market has grown substantially over the last few years," said Jack Zwingli, Standard & Poor's group vice president, adding that the market growth translated into increased demand for such an index. Large pension funds, for example, are now seriously considering investing in REIT's because market capitalizations have grown big enough to suit large institutional needs, S&P said in a statement.
The REIT Composite index is comprised of the three major types of REITS: equity, mortgage, and hybrid.
The index also reflects the property distribution of the REIT marketplace, S&P said.
